_doc: Cortex BEAM-10M FLAT-WRRF retrieval-proxy baseline. The TS cortex-beam-pg runner does FLAT recall (recall_memories top_k=10, no stage-aware context assembler), so it targets the FLAT-WRRF column, NOT the assembler column. Flat WRRF degrades with scale (the papers' thesis): 100K ~0.50, 500K 0.500, 1M 0.466, 10M 0.353. The context-assembly assembler adds ~+0.07 on top (10M ~0.429 with oracle stage labels) and is a SEPARATE, unported mechanism. METRIC: retrieval-proxy MRR (rank of first gold-matching memory), within-system comparison only, NOT BEAM's end-to-end LLM-as-judge. source: docs/arxiv-context-assembly flat-WRRF results provided by the owner 2026-06-22.

captured_from.metric_caveat: retrieval-proxy MRR; flat WRRF (no assembler); within-system only

_mrr_provenance.note: 0.523 is the current-code (2026-06-11) Cortex temporal-assembler reproduction; 0.471 was the 2026-04 paper snapshot; 0.353 is flat WRRF with no assembler. The TS port reproduces the current-code 0.523.
